chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalat ibn Ayyub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) at what age the child is taken for fasting. He (peace be upon him) said: Between fourteen and fifteen years of age. So if he fasts before that, let him be. And indeed, my son So-and-so fasted before that, so I let him do it.

key_terms.يُؤْخَذُ: is taken/accounted for (in terms of obligation)

ai.seo_question: At what age do children start fasting according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the preparatory stage of fasting (tadrib) for children, establishing the age of discernment (tamyiz) between fourteen and fifteen years as the threshold for formal obligation. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes a gradual, permissive approach, citing his own son’s early fasting as a precedent for encouraging practice before full maturity, thereby highlighting the pedagogical aspect of religious upbringing in Shia fiqh.
